data.name: Durga
data.gender_notes: Durga is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit durga, 'fort, a place difficult to reach' — 'the invincible one'. Its root is Sanskrit durga (दुर्ग). Durga, the warrior goddess who slays Mahishasura. Durga is a Sanskrit name meaning “Invincible; unassailable; the fort”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Durga expresses “Invincible; unassailable; the fort”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit durga, 'fort, a place difficult to reach' — 'the invincible one'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Durga total 24, reducing to 6. Number 6 is associated with responsibility, care and harmony.

vedic_reference.note: Durga is a central deity in the Hindu pantheon and is widely worshipped throughout India. She is often depicted as riding a lion or tiger, and holding weapons such as the trident, discus, conch shell, and bow and arrow. Durga is also known as 'Shakti', the goddess of power and strength.
